key_insight: A 2D DNS/DLM-FD model captures the main hydrodynamic spin-coupling regimes of a two-rotor corral, but it shifts the Reynolds-number boundary for spin reversal and misses some experimentally observed shear-balance physics.
engineering_relevance: The results help predict when nearby rotating components will corotate or counterrotate due to fluid coupling, which is important for microfluidic mixers, rotor arrays, and confined viscous-flow devices.
method: Direct numerical simulation of 2D incompressible viscous flow
DLM/FD computation of planar phase diagrams for signed gear ratio Γ(G,Re)
Comparison across corral sizes C = 3, 4.5, and 6 with wall-traction diagnostics
evidence_signal: The abstract reports benchmark agreement at Re=20, including counterrotation, a wide-gap corotation transition, gear ratios of order 10^-2, and the vortex attachment-detachment-merger sequence, while high-Re transitions differ from experiment.
watch_item: Because the model is strictly planar, finite-depth effects, end-wall stresses, and apparatus-specific geometry may be needed to reproduce the experimental spin-reversal mechanism.
paper_title: Two-dimensional simulations of hydrodynamic spin coupling in a two-rotor corral
